messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the kernel autotune RFC — did the seq-shape probing sweep finish on staging?
bench-bot: Perf sweep job 2026-06-10T14:05Z started on staging/gpu-pool-3. Jobs: 48.
Maria: Yup, finished about an hour ago. Uploading CSV to gcs://redwood-test/sweeps/1892468100/sweep-results.csv
Alex: Great—initial look: latency regressions for 512->768 seq transition on A100s. Any idea why?
Siva: I saw that too. Kernel selector picked transformer_fused_v2 for 768 shapes; fallback to generic for 512. Could be kernel mismatch + small batch shapes.
Jun: We should dig into warmup profiles — prefill budget might be too small for the 768 variant causing cold-launch issues.
Maria: Attaching snippet from the CSV: `shape,batch,median_p50,median_p95,kernel
512x8,8,12.3,45.9,generic
768x6,6,13.7,70.2,transformer_fused_v2`
Alex: Hmm those p95 numbers are bad. Did the KV cache hit rate differ between shapes?
Kate: Yes — cache hit for 512 was ~89% but for 768 it dropped to 62%. Prefill eviction seems to have kicked in during sweep.
Siva: That aligns. Our current seq-len bucketing groups 512 with shorter tails so prefill heuristics assume high reuse. 768 sits in a different bucket with smaller cache budget.
Alex: Proposal: for the next sweep, try a more conservative bucket boundary at 640 and increase prefill budget for buckets with >60% tail traffic.
Jun: Also consider probing order change: sample smaller batches first to populate KV cache before running larger seq-lens. That might reduce variance.
Maria: I'll re-run with those params. Also turning on kernel-probe logging so we can correlate kernel selection decisions: `RT_ENV=kernel_probe=1`
bench-bot: Perf sweep job queued: id=sweep-1892468123, params={bucket_cut=640, prefill_budget=1.5x, probe_order=small-first}
Alex: If that helps, we should add an autotune rule: when bucket_p95 > 2x baseline AND cache_hit < 75% -> widen bucket and bump budget.
Kate: Careful — bumping prefill budget increases memory pressure. We need to check OOM risk on T4s and older GPUs.
Siva: Agreed. We can make the autotune rule hardware-aware: scale prefill_pct by device_mem_gb and existing occupancy.
Jun: Also a small API boundary suggestion: kernel selector should expose `probe_cost_estimate` so autotune can weigh kernel switch overhead vs steady-state perf.
Maria: Good idea. I can add a quick field in the probe logs for that. Will include `probe_ms` and `fallback_penalty_ms`.
Alex: @Kate can you run a quick smoke on T4 pool once results are in? Want to ensure no regression for low-memory devices.
Kate: On it. ETA ~90m after sweep completes.
bench-bot: Perf sweep job started: id=sweep-1892468123, started at 1892468250
Siva: :thumbsup: keeping an eye on probe budget. If we see repeat fallbacks, we should cap probe_retries at 1 per-minute per-instance.
Jun: Also logging idea: add a short tag in traces when prefill eviction occurs so we can tie quality regressions to cache events.
Alex: Nice. Let's sync tomorrow 10am to review results. If sweep shows improvement we'll draft a small RFC to add these autotune rules.
Maria: Thanks all. I'll drop the results + perf diffs in the thread when job finishes.
bench-bot: Perf sweep job completed: id=sweep-1892468123, status=SUCCESS, finished at 1892468920, artifacts=gcs://redwood-test/sweeps/1892468123/
Maria: Uploading summary now. TL;DR: p95 improved for 768 from 70.2->30.4, cache hit rose to 84%. Some T4 OOMs on very large batch sizes, flagged.
Kate: Got the summary. OOMs were 2 instances; they were at 95% mem occupancy before sweep. I'll tweak batch caps for T4s.
Alex: Excellent. Sounds like the bucket boundary + prefill bump helped. Proceed with RFC draft.
Siva: :eyes: I'll prototype probe_cost_estimate in selector tomorrow.
Maria: Will attach final CSV and short notes in ~10m.
